queue.title: Corporate Governance for Family Businesses
queue.content:
No external shareholders doesn't remove the need for governance structure, it only delays the moment it's missed. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

The absence of external shareholders doesn't relieve a company of the need for a formal governance structure — it only delays the moment when its absence becomes visible.

The absence of external shareholders doesn't relieve a company of the need for a formal governance structure — it only delays the moment when its absence becomes visible.

Companies with concentrated or family ownership often skip formal governance mechanisms because the law doesn't directly require them in the absence of external shareholders.

That same absence of structure becomes an operational problem at the moment of growth, a new partner joining, generational change, or simply when the number of decisions exceeds the capacity of informal agreement.

Clearly defined roles, regular governance meetings with written minutes, and explicit decision-making rules don't restrict an owner — they protect business continuity independent of any one person.

The GNK DINAMO Ltd. Group publicly documents its governance structure precisely because transparency toward third parties requires prior internal clarity.

queue.title: Measuring Digitalization Return on Investment
queue.content:
Digitalization without a defined success metric easily becomes a cost justified by trend, not result. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

Digitalization without a defined success metric easily becomes a cost justified by trend, not by result.

Digitalization without a defined success metric easily becomes a cost justified by trend, not by result.

The decision to digitalize a process is often made based on expectations, but rarely subsequently measured against predefined, concrete success indicators.

Reduced processing time, error counts before and after, or actual labour-hour savings are more measurable indicators than a general claim that a process is now 'digitalized'.

Comparing the real implementation cost — including the team's hidden adjustment time — against the measured saving gives a more realistic picture than the initial projection made before the project began.

The practice of a post-implementation review, conducted three to six months after rollout, reveals whether expected benefits were actually realised or the project just changed the shape of the same problem.

queue.title: Ownership Succession and Business Continuity
queue.content:
Ownership transfer without a pre-agreed plan is the most common cause of continuity disruption. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

Ownership transfer without a pre-agreed plan remains the most common cause of continuity disruption in family and ownership-concentrated companies.

Ownership transfer without a pre-agreed plan remains the most common cause of continuity disruption in family and ownership-concentrated companies.

The moment of ownership change — whether planned or sudden — reveals whether governance authority, signing rights, and access to key systems were ever clearly documented independent of one person.

Companies that keep ownership concentrated in one or two people rarely formally test the scenario of their sudden unavailability, even though the operational risk is comparable to any other business continuity plan.

A practical approach includes a written succession plan for key authorities, clearly defined alternate signatories, and regularly updated system and account access lists that must not depend on one person's memory.

The GNK DINAMO Ltd. Group's ownership structure is documented through public registries precisely for that reason — structural transparency makes it easier for any third party to verify who actually makes the decisions.
